**Setup.** Let $X \sim \text{Bin}(41, 0.3)$ be Frank's number of wins in 41 games. Each match is decided within 41 games, since someone must reach 21 wins by then.

**Reduction.** Let $L$ be the number of games the loser wins before the match ends, so $E[N] = 21 + E[L]$.

If Frank wins the match with $j$ losses, the probability is $\binom{20+j}{j}p^{21}q^j$, where $p = 0.3$ and $q = 0.7$. Using $j\binom{20+j}{j} = 21\binom{20+j}{j-1}$ and reindexing, the Frank-wins contribution to $E[L]$ becomes

$$A = 21\cdot\frac{q}{p}\,P(X \ge 22).$$

By the symmetric argument, the Joe-wins contribution is

$$B = 21\cdot\frac{p}{q}\,P(X \le 19).$$

So

$$E[N] = 21 + 21\left[\frac{q}{p}P(X\ge 22) + \frac{p}{q}P(X\le 19)\right] = 21 + 49\,P(X\ge 22) + 9\,P(X\le 19).$$

(Check: for first-to-2 with $p=q=0.5$, this gives $2.5$, matching direct computation.)

**Numerics.** Using the binomial pmf for $X \sim \text{Bin}(41, 0.3)$:

- $P(X=22) \approx 0.000875$
- $P(X\ge 22) \approx 0.001324$
- $P(X=21) \approx 0.002246$, $P(X=20) \approx 0.005242$
- $P(X\ge 20) \approx 0.008812$, so $P(X\le 19) \approx 0.991188$

Then

$$E[N] \approx 21 + 49(0.001324) + 9(0.991188) \approx 21 + 0.0649 + 8.9207 \approx 29.99.$$

Frank's chance of winning the match is only about 0.36%, so the match almost always goes to Joe, and that is why the expected length is close to the maximum of 41.

ANSWER: ≈ 29.99
